sections.title: Diabetes and endocrine red flags
sections.alert: Diabetes or endocrine emergency: suspected DKA, HHS, severe hypoglycaemia, thyroid storm, myxoedema coma or adrenal crisis needs emergency care now; follow the protocol. An infected or ischaemic foot ulcer needs same-day referral to a diabetic foot team or vascular surgeon. Reduced vision in thyroid eye disease needs urgent ophthalmology review.

fields.label: Foot ulcer with spreading redness, swelling, pus, fever or crepitus (infection)
Foot ulcer or rest pain with absent pulses, or a pale, cold or dusky foot (ischaemia)
Hot, red, swollen foot with intact skin (possible active Charcot foot)
High glucose with vomiting, abdominal pain, deep fast breathing or ketones (possible DKA)
Very high glucose with marked dehydration, drowsiness or confusion (possible HHS)
Severe hypoglycaemia: needed help from another person, fits or unconsciousness
Hyperthyroid with fever, fast or irregular pulse, agitation or confusion
Hypothyroid with drowsiness, low temperature or slow pulse
Vomiting, low BP or collapse in a patient on long-term steroids or with adrenal insufficiency
Reduced vision or colour vision in thyroid eye disease
Stridor or rapidly enlarging neck swelling

advice.title: Caring for your feet
advice.text: Look at both feet every day, including between the toes, or ask someone to help. Do not walk barefoot, in socks only or in thin slippers, at home or outside. Feel inside your shoes before wearing them. Wash your feet daily in water that is not hot and dry well between the toes. Do not warm your feet with a heater or hot-water bottle. Do not cut corns yourself or use corn plasters. Use moisturiser, but not between the toes, and cut nails straight across. Show a doctor at once any blister, cut, scratch or sore.

advice.title: Low sugar (hypoglycaemia)
advice.text: If you feel shaky, sweaty, confused or suddenly hungry, check your sugar if you can and take glucose or sugar dissolved in water at once. Check again after 15 minutes and repeat if still low, then eat a snack or meal. Teach your family what to do. Tell your doctor about every low, and come at once if you needed help from someone or became unconscious.

advice.title: When you are unwell (sick-day rules)
advice.text: When you have fever, vomiting, diarrhoea or cannot eat, never stop your insulin. Check your sugar more often, and ketones if you have been told how. Drink plenty of fluids and ask your doctor which tablets to pause while unwell. Come to hospital at once if you keep vomiting or cannot keep fluids down, have abdominal pain, fast deep breathing, drowsiness or confusion, or your sugar stays very high.

advice.title: Thyroid treatment and tests
advice.text: Take your thyroid medicine every day as prescribed, even when you feel well. After a dose change it can take several weeks to months for symptoms to settle, so keep your blood test appointments. Tell your doctor if you take biotin (often in hair, skin and nail supplements), as it can make thyroid blood tests wrong.
